sentences.text: Bench : Hon'ble Shri Sanjay S. Agrawal, J Order On Board 01/10/2024 1)

By virtue of this petition, the petitioners have prayed for the following reliefs:-
i.

To kindly set aside the Land Acquisition Proceedings of Land Acquisition Case No.
08/A-82 year 2006-2007 as being lapsed.

ii. To kindly quash the award dated 19/11/2007 on the ground of being lapsed under the provisions of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
iii. To kindly direct the respondents to act afresh in accordance with the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: iv. To kindly make any other order that may be deemed fit and just in the facts and circumstances of the case including awarding of the costs to the petitioner.

2) According to the petitioners, though the award has been passed in the said acquisition proceeding and the amount of compensation, as determined, was paid to the petitioners, but the possession of their lands has, however, not been taken over,
therefore, the entire acquisition proceeding, as was initiated by the concerned Land Acquisition Officer, has lapsed by virtue of sub-section (2) of Section 24 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 2013").
3) On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the State/respondents while placing his reliance upon the principles as laid down by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the matter of Indore Development Authority v. Manoharlal and Others reported in (2020) 8 SCC 129, submits that since the amount of compensation determined by the Land Acquisition Officer has already been paid to the petitioners, therefore, the award dated 19/11/2007 passed in the said Land Acquisition Rajesh Patil vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163267272/

sentences.text: Proceedings cannot be quashed and/or held to be lapsed.
4) I have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the entire papers annexed with this petition.

5) From perusal of the record, it appears that the award was passed on 19/11/2007 in Land Acquisition Case No. 08/A-82 year 2006-2007, where, the amount of compensation, as reflected from the averments made by the petitioners, has been paid.

It is to be seen at this juncture, the principles laid down by Hon'ble the Supreme Court, in the matter of Indore Development Authority v. Manoharlal and Others (supra), wherein, the Supreme Court while interpreting the said provision prescribed under sub-section (2) of Section 24 of the Act, 2013 has held at paragraph 366.3 as under:-
"The word "or" used in Section 24(2) between possession and compensation has to be read as "nor"
or as "and".

entities.text: Indore Development Authority v. Manoharlal and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deemed lapse of land acquisition proceedings under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act takes place where due to inaction of authorities for five years or more prior to commencement of the said Act, the possession of land has not been taken nor compensation has been paid.

In other words,
in case possession has been taken, compensation has not been paid then there is no lapse.

Similarly,
if compensation has been paid, possession has not been taken then there is no lapse."

6) In view of the principles laid down by Hon'ble the Supreme Court, the alleged Land Acquisition Proceeding cannot be held to be lapsed as the amount of compensation determined by the Land Acquisition Officer has already been received by the petitioners.
7) Consequently, the petition being devoid of merit is dismissed.
No order as to cost(s).

Sd/-
(Sanjay S. Agrawal) JUDGE Prashant Rajesh Patil vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163267272/
